official.description_text:
Postdoc in complex fluid flows
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences
Job description
We are seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral to join the Fluids and Surfaces Group at KTH. The position offers the opportunity to develop an independent research profile within a broad range of topics, including turbulence, multiphase flows, interfacial phenomena, biofilms, surface engineering, computational fluid dynamics, and scientific machine learning.
The research direction will be adapted to the successful candidate’s expertise and interests. You will work closely with a dynamic team of PhD students and researchers and have access to unique experimental platforms, advanced numerical simulation tools, and high-performance computing resources. The position is supported by an ERC-funded research program, providing excellent opportunities to pursue ambitious research questions and establish international collaborations.
Your main duties will be to conduct high-quality research, publish in leading journals, contribute to the development of new research directions, and support the supervision of doctoral and master's students. Depending on your background, the work may involve experiments, direct numerical simulations, theoretical modelling, data-driven methods, or combinations thereof.
The FLOW center offers an internationally recognized research environment with strong expertise in fluid mechanics and applied mathematics. The division maintains extensive collaborations with leading academic institutions and industrial partners worldwide.
This position is particularly suitable for candidates who enjoy scientific challenges, value intellectual freedom, and wish to contribute to the development of next-generation approaches for understanding and controlling complex fluid systems.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
Demonstrated scientific expertise in fluid mechanics.
Ability to conduct independent research and publish scientific results in peer-reviewed journals.
Good collaborative skills and the ability to work in an international research environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, as it is required in the daily work
Research expertise
Teaching abilities
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
As a person, you are independent, proactive, and have a strong ability to collaborate with researchers and students.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Experience in supervision or teaching at the university level.
Experience of international research collaborations.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.

ai.summary: KTH postdoc in fluid mechanics, covering turbulence, multiphase flows, biofilms, computational fluid dynamics, and scientific machine learning. Position emphasizes independent research direction, experimentation or simulation, and collaboration within the FLOW center.

thematic_fit.rationale: Fluid mechanics, CFD, and applied mathematics have no connection to human-centred XR, collaborative immersive systems, spatial cognition, learning design, or wayfinding. Completely orthogonal research domain.

methodological_fit.rationale: Position requires expertise in experiments, numerical simulation, or theoretical modelling—none of which match the researcher's HCI/XR methodology (user studies, experimental design for spatial cognition, immersive system evaluation). Scientific machine learning could offer adjacent technical interest, but is incidental to the core work.

growth_value.rationale: Exposure to high-performance computing and data-driven methods could develop technical skills, but does not advance human-centred immersive systems research or close gaps in HCI/XR evaluation methodology.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH and Stockholm are geographically aligned; ERC funding indicates research stability. However, the Fluids and Surfaces Group research trajectory does not support entry into human-centred XR/HCI. Two-year postdoc would delay PhD pathway.

eligibility_flags: Requires PhD in fluid mechanics or closely related field. Researcher holds MSc in Creative Multimedia—significant disciplinary gap.
Requires PhD completion by employment decision date.
Preference for recent PhDs (within 3 years) aligns with 2026 completion.
risks: Severe disciplinary mismatch: Creative Multimedia background does not meet stated requirements in fluid mechanics/engineering.
Fundamental research domain misalignment: fluid dynamics is excluded by target identity exclusion list (pure technical engineering).
Career trajectory risk: two years in CFD/applied mathematics weakens HCI/XR positioning for future PhD applications.
